title: DUNE latent-prior scanner Mirror chart
hypothesis: On a synthetic scanner-shift reconstruction task, one Givens chart inside the DUNE latent regularizer improves held-out scanner-B reconstruction beyond native shared DUNE and byte-near FiLM while leaving exact decoder-VJP data consistency and final measurement projection unchanged.

prior_art.paper: Deep Unrolled Networks in Representation Space Applied to MRI Reconstruction
prior_art.repo_status: Public repository contains README only at observed commit; author says code will be available upon publication; no source license or checkpoints observed; implementation independently follows paper Eqs. 5, 6, 8.

model.representation: 4-channel learned feature representation from 2-channel complex SENSE image; shared 1x1 encoder and decoder
model.data_consistency: DUNE exact decoder VJP for A^H(A(D(z))-y) at each latent step. Final output is the orthogonal image-space projection onto A(x)=y, computed with a deterministic QR factorization of the explicit complex SENSE operator. The same sensitivity map, mask, operator factorization, and solve apply to every method; acquired-sample residual is measured by re-encoding the returned image.
model.mirror_insertion: scanner-B code is a Givens angle on latent channel pairs (0,1) and (2,3), conjugating only shared latent regularizer R_m(z)=T(-m)R(T(m)z). Encoder, decoder, forward operator, VJP, QR image-space projection, mask, coil maps, and data are unchanged.

data.type: analytic synthetic complex phantoms with two smooth coils; no acquired MRI
data.scanner_shift: known analytic coil sensitivity amplitude/phase shift; maps supplied as explicit forward operator; no shift is hidden from A
data.operator_rank_note: 2 coils x 14 sampled phase-encode lines x 32 readouts = 896 complex measurements < 1024 complex image unknowns, so the inverse problem remains underdetermined.

controls: native shared DUNE latent prior, frozen on scanner B
same DUNE plus scanner-specific latent FiLM scale+bias (8 coefficients)
DUNE plus scanner-specific latent Givens Mirror angle (1 coefficient)
full independent scanner-B fine-tune upper control

training.selection: one frozen architecture, no hyperparameter tuning; scanner-B support only updates Mirror/FiLM codes or full upper control; dev remains separate

metrics: CPU update and per-case wall time

storage.report: base DUNE payload; added scanner-B code payload; total two-scanner deployment payload compared with base plus independent full scanner-B model
storage.comparison: Serialize all alternatives with the same outer keys, architecture/operator metadata, dtype and deployment labels; only the paid model/code tensor structure differs. Measure complete torch.save inference/deployment payloads.

success_gate: Mirror improves dev NMSE at least 5% versus native shared DUNE and same-model FiLM, is within 10% of independent scanner-B fine-tune, saves at least 20% total serialized bytes against two independent scanner models, and projected acquired-sample residual <=1e-5.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the quality or storage gate, fails the measurement residual gate, or changes the decoder VJP/forward/projection path.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism only; no fastMRI, prototype scanner, patient, or clinical claim.
One coil-map shift and one train/dev split.
Repo has no released implementation/checkpoint at pinned observed commit; independently implemented from equations.

compute.projection: Operator QR factorization is reported as one-time wall and ephemeral bytes per unique sensitivity-map/mask pair; per-case inference timing starts after cache warmup and uses the same cached factors.

amendment_01.reason: Pre-metric operator test found 12 CG steps left relative acquired-sample residual 8.12e-2, failing registered 1e-5 gate. Increased common projection iterations to 256 (residual <1e-5 on fixed test) before training/evaluating any model; identical for all arms.

amendment_02.reason: The initial four-coil case had 1792 complex samples for 1024 complex image unknowns, so strict projection itself recovered the target and made the prior comparison non-identifying. Before any corrected quality run, reduce to two explicit coils: same 14 sampled lines now gives 896 < 1024 measurements. Preserve initial metrics separately as invalid; reuse fixed source/support/dev seed lists; fresh remains sealed.

amendment_03.reason: With the underdetermined two-coil A, object-space CG projection did not achieve the registered tolerance robustly (relative residual 2.7e-4 and then rose with iterations). Replace it with exact orthogonal projection in measured k-space: measured entries are set to y exactly, unmeasured entries remain the prior prediction; report the image re-encoded residual separately. This is identical for all conditions and is frozen before corrected quality results.

amendment_04.reason: Amendment 03 development metrics were identical because the k-space projection helper used a masked forward prediction, setting every unmeasured coefficient to zero before the projection. This masked the latent prior output. Preserve those invalid metrics. Before the corrected rerun, use the unmasked SENSE/FFT prediction for unacquired coefficients, replace only acquired coefficients by measured y, and apply the same SENSE adjoint. No fresh examples were accessed.

amendment_05.reason: Amendment 04 had zero projected k-space residual but the SENSE-adjoint image re-encoded with 6.9% residual, so it did not meet the exact image-space projection requirement. Before corrected metrics, use QR of A^H to compute the orthogonal projection x + Q(R^H)^-1(y-Ax); this is stable for the underdetermined full-row-rank operator and preserves the nullspace component. No fresh data accessed.

amendment_06.reason: The first quality run timed the one-time scanner-B QR construction only in the first method, making native per-case latency incomparable to later methods. Before the final replay, warm/cache the same operator factorization before timing every method, report one-time QR construction separately, and measure cached per-case latency. No model weights, codes, quality metrics, or seeds change.

failure_gate_result: FAIL: Mirror improves NMSE only 0.00060216% vs native shared and 0.00347974% vs FiLM, below 5% threshold. With uniform serialization, complete two-scanner payloads are 5,965 B hard shared, 6,217 B Mirror, 6,469 B FiLM, and 10,419 B independent. Mirror adds 252 B over hard sharing at effectively tied quality; fresh remains sealed.

amendment_07.reason: The interim byte audit revealed nonuniform metadata/container framing between standalone models and multi-scanner deployment objects. Before finalizing storage results, use a shared serialization schema with identical architecture/operator metadata and top-level keys for hard-shared, Mirror, FiLM, and independent two-scanner deployments; only paid model/code tensors differ. No quality metrics or model choices change; fresh remains sealed.
